tests.name: a verified PayPal email is accepted, ignoring case
an email PayPal has not verified is never accepted
a different PayPal account does not match the order
an emails list counts only if the primary one is confirmed
a refund event points at the refund id
payout item and batch events point at the payout batch id
other events, or events with no id, settle nothing
a failed, blocked or returned payout names the batch we stored, so the case can be reopened
a failed refund names the refund id, and PayPal's own error text is used when it sends one
unclaimed or held payouts are only noted, never treated as failures that allow a second payment
failure events with no id, and success events, are not failures
the first try and any try with an unknown outcome reuse the same PayPal request id
after a definite failure the retry gets a fresh request id, one more for each failure
a refund or payout is Settled only after PayPal's webhook, not when the request is accepted
replacements and repair kits are Settled at once, because PayPal sends no webhook for them
an open case is Notified until the buyer opens the notice, then Waiting
a refused or failed case shows as Problem, never as waiting or settled
before a decision, the path comes from the recall's remedy and the order's age
once the policy engine has decided, its action wins over the preview
emails are masked to the first letter and the domain
time ago reads in minutes, hours and days
the numbers count settled cases per path, and 'products fixed' is settled over affected
long timeline lines are cut to one line with an ellipsis, short ones are untouched
several orders of the same recall become one group, in order of first appearance
a refund past 180 days is described as a PayPal Payout, inside it as a refund; other remedies say nothing
the amount for several orders adds the prices; remedies with no money say Free
no recalls gives all zeros, not an error
online recalls are counted from the sold-online flag
Amazon is any recall whose retailers text mentions Amazon, in any letter case
a barcode counts as listed only when a UPC number is written out
a barcode that is only mentioned, with no number, does not count
a barcode number in the product list also counts
an order paid 179 days ago is refunded
an order paid exactly 180 days ago is still refunded (the window includes day 180)
one millisecond past 180 days switches to PayPal Payouts
an order paid 400 days ago is paid by Payouts, and the reason says so
a replacement adds tracking and moves no money
a repair records the kit request and moves no money
a buyer cannot pick a remedy the recall does not offer
no PayPal payment on record means no money, even inside the window
never pays more than the order total
rejects zero, negative or fractional amounts
refunds only the recalled item, not the whole order
